stem: Which Commission accentuated the discontent in all the political groups and parties for not associating any Indian member in it?
expl: In 1927, the British government appointed a statutory commission to review the provisions of the Government of India Act, 1919; it was called the Simon Commission. All seven members of this commission were British, and not even a single Indian representative from any Indian political party, group, community, or organization was included in it.

stem: When did Simon Commission visit India?
expl: In the Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms of 1919, there was a provision to set up a Statutory Commission for review after 10 years. The Commission had to examine how far this Act had been successful in practice and how much progress had been made towards responsible government. However, the Conservative government in Britain appointed the Simon Commission (Indian Statutory Commission) two years earlier itself, in November 1927. This commission was chaired by Sir John Simon and had a total of 7 members. Since all the members were British, the Congressmen opposed it by calling it a “White Commission.” The Simon Commission reached Bombay on 3 February 1928.

stem: Fill in the blanks— The Nehru Report was prepared by a committee under the chairmanship of ........... and its subject was .......... .

options.label: a
options.text: M otilal Nehru and Jawaharlal Nehru; India’s relationship with the British Empire

options.label: b
options.text: Jawaharlal Nehru; local self-government in India

options.label: c
options.text: Motilal Nehru; constitutional arrangements in India

options.label: d
options.text: Jawaharlal Nehru; constitutional arrangements in India

expl: Since no Indian was included in the Simon Commission, during the protests against the Commission in India, the Secretary of State for India, Lord Birkenhead, challenged the Indians and said that Indians were incapable of making concrete proposals for constitutional reforms. He said that Indians were unable to frame a constitution that could receive broad political support from all Indians. The Indians accepted this challenge, and to finalize this plan, all-party conferences were held in February, May and August, 1928. A committee of nine members under the chairmanship of Motilal Nehru (the total number of members, including the chairman, was 10) presented the draft of the proposed constitution in August, 1928. Later, it came to be known as the “Nehru Report” after Motilal Nehru. In it, the demand for separate electorates on a communal basis was rejected. This report demanded “Dominion Status”. Besides this, other recommendations were also made, such as: adult franchise for all, equal rights for women, freedom to form unions (associations), and separation of religion from the state in every respect.

stem: "Remember once again, now that this flag is unfurled, it must not be lowered as long as a single Indian, man, woman, or child lives in India." Who said this?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Jawaharlal Nehru said in Lahore: “Remember once again, now that this flag is unfurled; it must not be lowered as long as a single Indian man, woman, or child remains alive in India.” The Lahore Session of 1929 was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru. In this very session, the resolution of “Purna Swaraj” was passed, and it was decided to celebrate 26 January as Independence Day.

stem: The proposal of Purna Swaraj was passed in Lahore Congress in the year-
expl: In the Calcutta Session of the Congress, an ultimatum was given to the British Government that it should accept the Nehru Report by the end of the year, or else it would have to face a mass movement to be started by the Congress. When the government did not give any definite reply within the fixed time-limit, the historic Lahore Session of the Congress was held in December, 1929 under the presidentship of Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru, in which Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru declared the objective of Purna Swaraj (Complete Independence). As the midnight hour struck on 31 December, 1929, the Congress President, Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru, unfurled the flag of Indian independence on the banks of the Ravi River at Lahore. In its meeting on 2 January, 1930, the Congress Working Committee decided that 26 January, 1930 would be celebrated as “Purna Swadhinata Diwas” or “Purna Swaraj Diwas”. From here, the celebration of 26 January every year as Complete Independence Day began.
